claims.text: Nepal's government requested specialized foreign assistance including tunnel rescue teams, locate technology, rapid forensic DNA analysis, and mortuary facilities.
An 11-member technical reconnaissance team for tunnel rescue from India was deployed to Nepal, with a Chinese tunnel rescue team expected shortly.
Disaster agencies reported nearly 3,000 people missing, including 2,426 in Nepal and 554 in Tibet.
The missing list from the flood included at least 777 foreign nationals and 933 workers from hydropower projects along the affected river.
The total confirmed death toll reached 682, comprising 675 dead in Nepal and seven confirmed dead in Tibet.
The Red Cross estimated that more than 3,700 people were rescued in Nepal, while at least 93,000 people were affected by the catastrophe.
Nepali army rescuers pumped air through pipes into tunnels at the Trishuli 3A and 3B hydropower sites to supply trapped workers.
Nepalese Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha stated that a hole was drilled into a cable tunnel, but no contact was established with trapped personnel.
The US State Department pledged an initial $500,000 in emergency humanitarian aid for Nepal.
The US Geological Survey attributed the high-altitude border disaster to a massive glacial collapse that triggered downstream debris torrents.
Nepalese Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi agreed to increase real-time sharing of hydrological and satellite data.
Nepalese Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal highlighted that Nepal produces approximately 0.01 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions despite suffering severe impacts.
UN climate chief Simon Stiell stated that a warming climate driven by fossil fuel burning makes mountain disasters more frequent and severe.
Flood survivors in Nuwakot district publicly criticized the Nepalese government for delays in delivering relief aid and searching for missing persons.
India's Ministry of External Affairs revised down the number of missing Indian nationals in Nepal to 287 on Saturday evening.
India's Ministry of External Affairs reported that 128 people of Indian origin holding other nationalities remained uncontactable in Nepal.
Indian authorities reported rescuing 88 Indian nationals in Nepal, including four hydropower workers extracted from a site in Rasuwa.
120 Indian nationals crossed the border from Tibet into Nepal on Saturday following the flood disruption.
Chinese authorities in Gyirong port evacuated 555 tourists and relocated 499 local villagers and workers to safety.
Chinese hydrological monitoring confirmed that a major dammed debris lake began naturally draining, reducing immediate outburst flood risks.
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat delivered a keynote address at the 'Universal Oneness Celebration' hosted by AHEAD at Madison Square Garden in New York.
Mohan Bhagwat stated that if any Hindu believes there should be no Muslims in India, that person ceases to be a Hindu.
Mohan Bhagwat cited RSS volunteers' relief work following the 1996 Charkhi Dadri mid-air collision in Haryana to emphasize non-discriminatory service.
Mohan Bhagwat spoke to community and interfaith leaders at the 'One World, One Humanity' conference in New York City on August 29, 2026.
Mohan Bhagwat stated that RSS volunteers currently run approximately 130,000 community service projects.
Mohan Bhagwat noted that the RSS intensified outreach and dialogue with Muslim and Christian communities in India starting in 2018.
The Universal Oneness Celebration at Madison Square Garden was supported by over 200 Hindu American organizations.
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani expressed strong opposition to the RSS event, labeling the organization's ideology as exclusionary.
The US Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) recommended revoking Mohan Bhagwat's visa and imposing sanctions on RSS members.
Mohan Bhagwat arrived in the United States on Tuesday as part of an RSS centenary-year outreach tour covering North America and the UK.
Civil rights, interfaith, and caste advocacy groups staged protests outside Madison Square Garden opposing Mohan Bhagwat's appearance.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi previously addressed an audience of 50,000 people during the 2019 'Howdy, Modi!' event in Texas.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Uzbekistan on Saturday for a two-nation Central Asian visit prior to attending the 26th SCO Summit in Bishkek.
Narendra Modi stated his intent to hold discussions with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev on trade, investment, digital connectivity, defense, and energy.
Modi's itinerary in Tashkent included visits to the Shastri Memorial and the Mahatma Gandhi Centre at Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies.
India's Ministry of External Affairs confirmed that Narendra Modi will hold a bilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the margins of the SCO Summit.
Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev personally greeted Prime Minister Modi upon his late-night arrival at Tashkent airport.
Prime Minister Modi's aircraft took a detour through Chinese airspace because Pakistani airspace remained closed to Indian aircraft.
Modi laid a floral wreath at Yangi Uzbekistan Park in Tashkent shortly after his arrival.
Uzbekistan hosts more than 18,000 Indian residents, including approximately 16,000 medical students.
Prime Minister Modi scheduled attendance at the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games in Kyrgyzstan during his tour.
This trip marks Narendra Modi's fourth official visit to Uzbekistan, following trips in 2015, 2016, and 2022.
The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation consists of 10 member states spanning 36 million square kilometers and a population exceeding 3.4 billion people.
The SCO accounts for approximately 25 percent of global gross domestic product and over 15 percent of international trade.
